input.question: Why are the U.S. Navy's uniforms pixelated?
input.ground_truth: It's actually to reduce the visibility of paint and grease on the uniforms. It's camouflage for what gets on the uniform, not for the person wearing it. As a Marine you no doubt know the military can be pretty strict on standards for a serviceable uniform, and sailors work in dirty areas and paint a lot, so it reduces replacement costs. As far as falling overboard, if you're not wearing a flotation device (which are IIRC safety orange) you're at best neck or shoulder-deep. What you're wearing has far less effect on your visibility than your movement or any signaling you can do.
